metadata.note: 2m: state 2 properties of EM waves. 2 slots, 1m each. Multiple correct properties: all travel at same speed in vacuum (3×10⁸ m/s), transverse waves, can travel through vacuum (no medium), transfer energy, obey laws of reflection/refraction.

question.name: CSEC Phy Jun 2023 Q3a — State Two Properties of EM Waves
question.general_feedback:
Properties of electromagnetic waves (any 2):

  • All travel at the same speed in vacuum — c = 3.0 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹ (the speed of light)
  • They are transverse waves — oscillations are perpendicular to the direction of travel
  • They can travel through a vacuum — they do not require a material medium to propagate
  • They transfer energy — without transferring matter
  • They obey the laws of reflection and refraction

groups.label: Property 1 of all electromagnetic waves
groups.diagnostic_hint: All EM waves travel at 3 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹ in a vacuum (the speed of light). They are TRANSVERSE waves that can travel through a vacuum (unlike sound waves).

ddwtos.word_bank_note: 6 tokens for 2 slots. 4 correct properties — any 2 of 4 earn full marks. 'They require a medium to travel' is the critical false token: this describes mechanical waves (sound, water waves), NOT EM waves. EM waves specifically DO NOT need a medium. 'They are longitudinal waves' is wrong — EM waves are transverse (oscillations perpendicular to direction of travel); sound is the classic longitudinal wave.
